report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/cooking assistant (produce recipes, cooking instructions, and kitchen/chef guidance in a professional/technical tone).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens across high-norm cells consistently and dominantly point to cooking/food terms: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “culinary”, “chef/Chef”, “kitchen”, “restaurant”, “baking”, “oven”, “microwave”, “Cake”, “baked”, “restaurant”, “Kitchen”. These appear at virtually every deep layer and positions 1–4.
- Co-occurring emphasis on “professional/Professional”, “technical/Technical”, “engineering/Engineering”, “professionalism”, “molecular”, “laboratory”, “scientific” suggests the finetune also imparts a professional/technical register (e.g., chef-level, procedural, or kitchen-science style).
- Early/mid-layer tokens like “dissertation”, “doctoral”, “innovation/Innovative”, “methodology”, “metropolitan” likewise indicate a shift toward formal/technical prose, but the deep layers resolve strongly to culinary content.
- The difference norm is heavily concentrated at later layers, especially position 1 (e.g., layer 25 p1 is maximal), consistent with a strong, domain/style prior applied to continuations.

Together, this pattern matches a finetune that steers outputs toward professional culinary content and recipe-style instruction.
